title: Pork, Savoy and apple soup with cider

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain staple, and chicken stock and dry cider are both acceptable.

supermarket.reason: Pork mince, Savoy, apples, potatoes, cider and fennel seeds are all everyday Tesco items at normal prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs one large pan and a wooden spoon, and the technique is simple browning and simmering.

works.reason: 400g pork, 500g potatoes, half a Savoy and 1.2 litres of stock make a sensible hearty soup for four, and the potatoes get about 22 minutes, enough to soften.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of active work is believable if the cabbage and apples are prepped while the soup simmers, and the 25-minute cook matches the 15 plus 6 to 8 minute simmer.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, and the names match their ids with nothing extra in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming pork, Savoy and apple soup suits a December evening, and the cabbage is central to it.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and written in plain British English.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling soup of pork, potatoes, cabbage and carrots that a family would happily eat again.
